advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a ConfigError from load_config in p4_oversize does not fail open to abstain in run_det_floor (resolve the limit outside the fail-open check, or make the DET wrapper propagate ConfigError), and cover the run_det_floor path in tests.
evidence: gate_ops.py:79 completion path: `description_limit = _config.load_config(ctx.repo_root)...` at top level (propagates)
test_ticket_description_limit.py `test_p4_does_not_hide_invalid_typed_configuration` invokes `p4_oversize(...)` directly, not through `run_det_floor`, so it does not exercise the swallowing path
advisory.finding: In a real plan-review run, `p4_oversize` calls `_description_limit()` -> `load_config()` from inside a DET check, but `run_det_floor` wraps every check in `try/except Exception` and converts a raised exception into an `abstain` (fail-open). So an invalid/ConfigError-raising config silently DISABLES the P4 description block during plan review, while `completion_precheck` calls `load_config` at top level (gate_ops.py:79) and propagates the error. The two admission gates disagree on invalid config, and the test `test_p4_does_not_hide_invalid_typed_configuration` calls `p4_oversize` directly, bypassing this swallowing path.
scenarios: An operator sets an out-of-range or malformed `verify.max_ticket_description_chars`; plan-review silently stops enforcing the description limit instead of surfacing the config error

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the new default-8000 description block is an intended unversioned breaking change (previously-valid tickets rejected at claim + close) and provide a disable toggle or migration path, or document/gate it behind an opt-in like the other verify.* gates.
evidence: det_floor.py p4_oversize now sets `blocking=description_over_limit` where previously P4 never set blocking (docstring: "P4/P6/P7 ... are advisory") and the old threshold `P4_DESC_SOFT_CAP_CHARS = 24_000` was advisory-only

gate_ops.py:81 `if description_chars > description_limit:` returns `{"run_verify": False, "precheck_failed": True, ... "verdict": verdict}` — a NEW deterministic FAIL short-circuit in completion_precheck that did not exist before (the arm precedes the pre-existing child_closure_findings gate at gate_ops.py:113)

Consumer/callsite (plan-review): workflow_ops.py:129-152 surfaces det_blocking from det_blocking_findings; the DET short-circuit at workflow_ops.py:154 guarantees a BLOCK verdict for any P4-description block, so claim of a previously-passing >8000-char ticket now fails

Consumer/callsite (completion close): gate_ops.py completion_precheck is the completion gate step; deterministic_child_failure(canonical, [finding], cfg, summary=oversize_summary) at gate_ops.py:104 yields a FAIL verdict skipping the LLM

The block is unconditional: config sets only the threshold (default 8000, _config_schema.py:152); no boolean enable/disable toggle exists, and the bug-tier arm explicitly preserves the P4 block (workflow_ops.py:136 `finding["criteria"] == ["P4"]`)
docs/config.md states force "does not make the oversized description pass either review gate" — confirming no bypass/migration path for the narrowed input
advisory.finding: New always-on blocking admission limit (verify.max_ticket_description_chars, default 8000) narrows previously-valid input at two public gates: ticket descriptions that previously PASSED the plan-review claim gate (P4 was advisory; old soft cap 24,000, never blocking) and reached the completion close verifier now BLOCK/FAIL deterministically. Existing projects with 8,001–24,000-char descriptions break at claim, and any description >8000 breaks at close, with no config toggle to disable the block and no version gate.
scenarios: An existing project claims a work ticket whose description is 12,000 chars (previously advisory-only, passed) — the claim now BLOCKs on P4
A parent/work ticket with a >8000-char description that previously ran the completion verifier and could close now FAILs the completion close gate deterministically before any LLM runs
